question: Should OpenClaw adopt the proposed immutable, session-persisted `sessions_spawn.tools` policy as the public capability-control contract for native subagents?
rationale: This is an additive but security-sensitive public tool-policy surface whose persistence and deny semantics determine long-term compatibility; source review cannot choose that product contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve the persisted policy direction
options.body: Keep the `tools` union as the public contract, then require current-head proof and clean merge resolution before landing.

options.title: Narrow to allow-only or none
options.body: Avoid deny/complement semantics for the first version and defer broader policy composition to a separately approved design.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Keep the canonical issue open for a dedicated security and product design decision before accepting a persisted per-session capability API.

recommendation.title: Approve the persisted policy direction
recommendation.body: Keep the `tools` union as the public contract, then require current-head proof and clean merge resolution before landing.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR author identifies this reviewer’s guidance as the basis for the current API redesign.
